title: Repair the Broken fstab
description: A one-field orphan line is breaking fstab parsing; replace it with a valid 6-field mount entry.
scenario: A cloud-init script crashed halfway through editing /etc/fstab and left a lone '//10.0.0.30/share' line with no mount point, no type and no options. fstab requires exactly six whitespace-separated fields per entry, and admins double-check the file with an awk field count before any reboot. Replace the orphan with the intended entry: /dev/sdb1 mounted on /mnt/data as ext4 with defaults and pass number 2.
symptoms: `mount -a` (and every boot) aborts with an fstab parse error
The last line of /etc/fstab contains only '//10.0.0.30/share'
The intended data disk /dev/sdb1 on /mnt/data was never mounted
Ops policy: no reboot while any fstab line has other than 6 fields
mission: Replace the orphan line in /etc/fstab with `/dev/sdb1 /mnt/data ext4 defaults 0 2` so every non-comment line has exactly 6 fields.

hints.title: The six fields
hints.content: fstab lines are: device, mount point, filesystem type, options, dump freq, pass no. — e.g. `/dev/sdb1 /mnt/data ext4 defaults 0 2`.

hints.title: Field-count check
hints.content: `awk '!/^#/ && NF>0 { if (NF!=6) bad=1 } END { exit bad }' /etc/fstab` exits non-zero while any line is malformed — the runbook's pre-reboot gate.

hints.title: Replace the whole line
hints.content: `sudo sed -i 's|^//10.0.0.30/share$|/dev/sdb1 /mnt/data ext4 defaults 0 2|' /etc/fstab` swaps the orphan for the correct entry in one shot.

acceptance_criteria.description: every non-comment fstab line has exactly 6 fields
the repaired entry mounts /dev/sdb1 on /mnt/data as ext4
the repaired entry ends with pass number 2
